about: This Merlot carries the name of Chelsea Goldschmidt, one of the five children of Nick and Yolyn Goldschmidt, New Zealanders who settled in Healdsburg in 1990. Nick was chief winemaker at Simi, then ran winemaking for Allied Domecq and Beam Estates, and he has long argued that Alexander and Dry Creek valleys are ideal ground for Merlot and Cabernet. Chelsea, along with her sisters Hilary and Katherine, has become a winemaker under her father’s mentoring, and each sister has a wine named for her.

The fruit comes from Guidestone Rise, a single vineyard in Alexander Valley, the warm, broad valley of the upper Russian River north of Healdsburg. Like all the family’s wines it is a single-vineyard, single-variety bottling made in small lots, in keeping with Nick’s motto of “one vintage, one vineyard, one variety.” Wine Spectator has reviewed the Guidestone Rise Merlot year after year, describing it as fleshy and fresh, with dark plum and red-fruit flavors.

By 2026 the 2017 has had nearly a decade in bottle. Expect red raspberry, black cherry and spice on the nose, and a full, round palate of plum, red currant, blackberry and bay leaf. Wine Spectator gave the 2017 89 points when it was released. With age, Merlot’s fresh fruit tends to soften toward savory, herbal and earthy notes, which suits grilled and wood-roasted meats.
facts: Released around 2019; now almost 10 years from harvest
